wars.name: Cisalpine Gallic revolt (200-197 BC)
wars.outcome: 'By 200 BC the Cenomani had gone over to the anti-Roman side', joining the Boii and Insubres in the assault on Placentia; in 197 Roman envoys secured at least their neutrality and 'the Insubres were routed'. The Cenomani lost no land; their treaty after 197 barred them from Roman citizenship, and in 187 an order to give up their arms was reversed on appeal to the Senate.
wars.note: The page names neither a Battle of Cremona nor of the Mincio.

certainty.note: The Po, the Oglio, the Alpine foothills and the Tartaro or Adige are the only limits the page gives.
